newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index ends 3.19 pct down in jittery trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index ends 3.19 pct down in jittery trade.

text.p: Bombay shares suffered heavy losses in jittery trade on Monday as a near-panic situation prevailed in the market, dealers said.
"Foreign funds are sellers in many pivotals. The market is in a free fall with emergence of no buyers even at these lower levels," said a dealer.

The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) tumbled 161.40 points or 5.2 percent in mid-day after settling higher by close. The benchmark index was down 98.86 points or 3.19 percent to a provisional 3,002.41 close.

Former premier P.V. Narasimha Rao won a temporary reprieve after the Supreme Court withheld its decision on whether to agree to a request by the Delhi police for a shift in venue on security grounds for a court cases against him.
"Political worries are pulling down the market," said Sunil Kothari of brokers Nagindas S. Kothari.

Meanwhile, the New Delhi High court deferred a ruling on a request by Rao for legal protection against arrest in a forgery case and said a non-bailable warrant for Rao's arrest issued last Friday will continue to remain temporarily suspended.
The NSE index lost 31.01 points to a provisional 872.96.
Traders said bank stock SBI led the fall in front-benchers after the central bank imposed a 24 percent cap on foreign holdings in the stock.
SBI shed 11.20 rupees to 217.25 at the BSE. It dropped 14.45 rupees to 217.30 at the NSE in volumes of 2.65 billion shares.

Bajaj Auto, Hindalco, ITC, Indian Hotels and Grasim figured among the pivotals that bore the selling pressure. Other market majors such as Reliance, TISCO and TElCO bucked the trend in early deals, but ended lower.
